answer: To deter Sybil attacks, agents must commit collateral at a designated protocol summit that verifies each identity. This bond ensures that misbehaving nodes cannot simply wander through the peer-to-peer layer undetected. If an attacker attempts to flood the network with a gale of fraudulent identities, the linear scaling of required deposits imposes a massive capital barrier, forcing the adversary to forfeit significant value upon detection of malicious consensus manipulation.
